items.title: Cinematic Dark Fantasy Scene of Elemental Collision
items.prompt: A cinematic dark fantasy scene of the uploaded reference character seated in a basement at the exact point where opposite elemental forces are born from their own body. Likeness Integrity (CRITICAL) Preserve the exact identity of the uploaded character. Maintain exact proportions, eye shape, spacing, stylization, silhouette, and material identity. Do not humanize. Do not reinterpret anatomy. Do not modify facial structure. Do not add unintended accessories. Identity must remain instantly recognizable. Core Scene The character is sitting in a melancholic, emotionally heavy pose at the center of a cold unfinished basement. From one open palm, molten lava pours downward in a continuous glowing stream. From the other open palm, freezing ice and frost pour downward in a continuous crystalline stream. Both elements spill onto the basement floor and form two separate flowing rivers: one lava river, one ice river. They travel across the concrete floor in opposite directions and meet nearby in the same scene. Elemental Interaction Where the rivers meet, the collision creates violent physical contrast: steam, glowing cracks, frost bloom, blackened wet concrete, cooling rock, and frozen shards. The meeting point must feel emotionally symbolic, like two inner states colliding. Creature Creation Story (CRITICAL) The lava and ice pouring from the palms are actively creating creatures on the floor. These creatures must feel born from the flowing material itself, not placed into the scene afterward. Some creatures are still forming out of the streams. Some are fully shaped and wandering around the seated character. Lava creatures: glowing, semi-molten, ember-veined, heat-distorted silhouettes. Ice creatures: translucent, frosted, crystalline, sharp-edged, cold-vapor silhouettes. They should vary in size and animals language, all kind of animals and insects. A few lava and ice creatures are already surrounding the character in quiet loyalty or silent observation. Character Pose & Emotion The character is seated, still, introspective, emotionally exhausted. Head slightly lowered. Shoulders carrying invisible weight. Palms open and angled downward so the lava and ice pour naturally from them. The pose must feel like grief, restraint, and power at the same time. Not a triumphant spellcasting pose. Not action-hero energy. Quiet sorrow. Controlled destruction. Environment A dark basement interior with: unfinished concrete floor, aged walls, pipes and exposed structure, subtle moisture stains, minimal objects, deep negative space. The basement should feel real, sparse, and slightly abandoned. The elemental rivers become the main environmental storytelling device. Camera & Perspective Use a low cinematic perspective, slightly below the seated character's eye line. Lens: 24mm or 28mm. The camera is close enough to feel intimate but wide enough to show the rivers spreading across the floor and the creatures surrounding the character. Composition should be slightly off-center, not symmetrical. Use foreground depth with one or two blurred creatures or fragments near the lens. The seated character remains the emotional anchor. Depth of Field Primary focal plane locked on the character's face, upper torso, and both pouring palms. Nearest creatures and the river collision point can remain slightly readable. Foreground and far background fall progressively out of focus. No full-frame sharpness. Lighting Main light: a weak cool basement lamp overhead, dim and emotionally cold. Ambient: dark blue low-light atmosphere throughout the basement. Secondary light comes naturally from the lava itself, casting warm orange-red underlight onto parts of the character and nearby creatures. Ice contributes faint cold reflections and subtle blue-white edge highlights. Lighting must stay directional and cinematic, with deep shadow mass and controlled contrast. No flat lighting. Color Grade Dominant palette: dark blue, cold grey, black shadow. Accents: molten orange-red from lava, pale cyan-blue from ice. The warm and cool elements must remain clearly separated and emotionally readable. Controlled saturation, cinematic highlight roll-off, no color flooding. Atmosphere Thin basement haze. Steam rising where lava and ice meet. Cold vapor around the ice creatures. Subtle airborne dust catching the weak overhead lamp. The air should feel heavy and lonely. Mood Melancholic. Mythic but grounded. The scene should feel like inner conflict externalized into the physical world. The character is not commanding the creatures. They are simply emerging from what the character cannot hold inside. Negative Constraints No heroic battle pose. No cheerful fantasy lighting. No flat basement rendering. No symmetrical centered composition. No generic fireballs or magic aura. No full-body sharpness. No random clutter. No cute cartoon expression unless it already belongs to the character identity.
